chapter_title: The Gupta Era: An Age of Tireless Creativity

concepts.title: The Gupta Dynasty and Its Realm
concepts.definition: From the fourth century CE the Gupta dynasty, with centres at Pataliputra and later Ujjayini, ruled much of northern India; peace, tribute and trade made their era one of tireless creativity.
concepts.key_idea: Stable rule freed hands and minds: when granaries and roads are safe, art and science flourish.

concepts.title: Kalidasa and Sanskrit Literature
concepts.definition: The Gupta era crowned Sanskrit letters: Kalidasa's plays and poems, including Raghuvamsham quoted in the chapter, set a standard of beauty and feeling that later centuries kept studying and imitating.
concepts.key_idea: A golden age speaks through its poets: Kalidasa's lines still teach that wisdom, not luxury, strengthens a kingdom.

concepts.title: Gupta Science, Mathematics and Nalanda
concepts.definition: Gupta India computed the solar year, explored astronomy and medicine, and carried mathematics forward towards the decimal place-value system; universities such as Nalanda drew students from far lands.
concepts.key_idea: The age measured the world: from eclipses to digits, Gupta learning reached far beyond its borders.

concepts.title: Gupta Art, Temples and Iron
concepts.definition: The age raised the first stone temples, painted the Ajanta caves with matchless murals, and cast the rust-resistant iron pillar at Delhi, evidence of engineering skill beside artistic genius.
concepts.key_idea: Creativity in stone, paint and metal: Gupta art gave India forms of beauty and craft it never lost.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Why is the Gupta period called a golden age?

solution_template.explain: Peace, trade, Sanskrit classics, mathematics, astronomy, temples and painting all flowered together.
Creativity across so many fields at once justifies the name, though many regions outside the realm had their own genius.
